units.translation: 1 the words ἀφ’ οὗ — Ἀρκαδία are read after Τεγέας, transposed by W and Wil. | 3 the lacuna is to be filled with the name of the father (Λυκούργου or cf. Apoll. Bibl. I 67), indicated by W

164. Ancaeus: Ancaeus and Epochus were sons of Lycurgus and Antinoe; Lycurgus is honored among the Arcadians, as Aristomenes says (M. IV 336). Homer also mentions this Lycurgus (H 142–45): ‘τὸν Λυκόοργος — ὑποφθὰς δουρὶ μέσον περόνησε’. And a festival called Moleia is held among the Arcadians, because Lycurgus, having lain in ambush during the battle, captured Ereuthalion; for molos means battle.
5 Apoll. Bibl. III 105 | Paus. VIII 4, 10 | 11 sch. 769/73 | sch. Theocr. I 124a
5 Ἔποχος in K : ἐπίοχος | 6 ὁ λυκ. in P : omitted in L | Ἀριστοτέλης proposed by Mueller | 9 rather Ἀρηίθοον, cf. H 136 sqq.

168–70. βῆ δ’ ὅγε Μαιναλίης: Maenalus is a mountain and city of Arcadia, named after Maenalus the Arcadian, whose father was Lycaon. καλιῇ is used instead of οἰκίᾳ, but properly it means a dwelling made of wood; κάλα are pieces of wood. For in ancient times they used wooden houses, since stone ones had not yet been devised.
sch. Pind. Ol. IX 88c | Paus. VIII 3, 4 | Steph. Byz. Μαίναλος | 12 Hesych. καλιήν | Et. M. 485, 51 | Et. Gud. 295, 3
14 supplied by R

172–73. βῆ δὲ καὶ Αὐγείης: He was by birth the son of Helius, but by adoption the son of Phorbas, from Hyrmine daughter of Neleus; but some say he was from the daughter of Nycteus, and others that she was the daughter of Epeius. Rays seem to flash from his eyes. Heracles cleansed the dung of his cattle.
15 Apoll. Bibl. II 88 | Paus. V 1, 6 | Hyg. Fab. 14 (46, 26)
15 γόνῳ in K : λόγῳ | 16 ἐπίκλησιν δὲ in L : τῇ δὲ ἀληθείᾳ in P | 17 Φυκτέως by Wil. from sch. Pind. | Ἐπειοῦ in K : ἐπόχου
176. Ἀστέριος δέ: He means Asterion. From Hyperasius, king of Achaea, the city Hyperesia is named. Homer (B 573): ‘οἵ θ’ Ὑπερασίην’.
20 Hyg. Fab. 14 (47, 1 Schm.) | 23 sch. A B 574 | Steph. Byz. Πελλήνη | Plin. Nat. hist. IV 20
20 Ὑπερ- everywhere in PH : Ὑπερρ- in L
177. Πελλήνης: The Achaean Pellene is spelled with ε, but the other one, in
Arcadia, is spelled with α, Pallene. Achaeis is a part of Thessaly, to which Pellene belongs.

179. Taenarum is a promontory of Laconia, named after Taenarus son of Poseidon.

181. Europa was the daughter of Tityus, son of Elara. He is punished in Hades because he seized Leto as she was going to Pytho, as Homer also says (λ 576): ‘Τιτυὸν Γαίης υἱόν’. But Euphorion (fg 123 Scheidw.) says that he was beloved of Artemis and is punished for that reason.
